title: Unit 4 · Shopping and clothes
description: Clothing, colours, demonstratives, preferences, sizes, prices, and useful shop language.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 4 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.translation: I am wearing a white shirt.
cards.note: Una camisa is a shirt.

cards.translation: She is wearing a T-shirt.
cards.note: Una camiseta is a T-shirt.

cards.translation: These trousers are black.
cards.note: Pantalones is normally plural.

cards.translation: The red skirt is very pretty.
cards.note: Una falda is a skirt.

cards.translation: I prefer the blue dress.
cards.note: Un vestido is a dress.

cards.translation: I need a jacket because it is cold.
cards.note: Una chaqueta is a jacket.

cards.translation: I wear a coat in winter.
cards.note: Un abrigo is a coat.

cards.translation: I am looking for comfortable shoes.
cards.note: Zapatos is plural here, so cómodo becomes cómodos.

cards.translation: When it rains, I wear boots.
cards.note: Las botas are boots.

cards.translation: When it is sunny, I wear a hat.
cards.note: Un sombrero is a hat.

cards.translation: The scarf protects the neck.
cards.note: Una bufanda is a scarf.

cards.translation: I keep the phone in the bag.
cards.note: Un bolso is a handbag or bag.

cards.translation: I have a red T-shirt.
cards.note: Roja agrees with the feminine noun camiseta.

cards.translation: He is wearing black shoes.
cards.note: Negros agrees with the masculine plural noun zapatos.

cards.translation: I am looking for two white shirts.
cards.note: Blancas agrees with the feminine plural noun camisas.

cards.translation: I like the green skirt.
cards.note: Verde has the same singular form for masculine and feminine nouns.

cards.translation: I prefer the blue trousers.
cards.note: Azul becomes azules in the plural.

cards.translation: She is wearing a brown jacket.
cards.note: Marrón has the same singular form for masculine and feminine nouns.

cards.translation: This shirt here is inexpensive.
cards.note: Esta agrees with the feminine singular noun camisa.

cards.translation: This coat here is new.
cards.note: Este agrees with the masculine singular noun abrigo.

cards.translation: These shoes here are comfortable.
cards.note: Estos agrees with the masculine plural noun zapatos.

cards.translation: That skirt there is pretty.
cards.note: Esa refers to a feminine singular noun at some distance.

cards.translation: Those boots there are expensive.
cards.note: Esas agrees with the feminine plural noun botas.

cards.translation: Which do you prefer, the red one or the blue one?
cards.note: Preferir changes e to ie in the tú form.

cards.translation: I prefer the blue one.
cards.note: Preferir changes e to ie in the yo form.

cards.translation: We prefer the small shop.
cards.note: The stem does not change in the nosotros form.

cards.translation: I like the black jacket better.
cards.note: Gustar más expresses liking one option better.

cards.translation: I have to take a jacket.
cards.note: After tener que, use an infinitive.

cards.translation: What do I have to take?
cards.note: Tener que + infinitive expresses obligation.

cards.translation: Today I am wearing a white shirt.
cards.note: Llevar means to wear in this context.

cards.translation: She is wearing a green dress.
cards.note: Lleva is the third-person singular of llevar.

cards.translation: What size do you need?
cards.note: La talla is the clothing size.

cards.translation: I need a medium size.
cards.note: Mediana means medium when describing the feminine noun talla.

cards.translation: How much does this T-shirt cost?
cards.note: Costar changes o to ue in the present tense.

cards.translation: How much do these shoes cost?
cards.note: Use cuestan with a plural subject.

cards.translation: It is too expensive.
cards.note: Demasiado caro means too expensive.

cards.translation: It is on sale; it is very inexpensive.
cards.note: Barato means inexpensive.

cards.translation: Can I try it on?
cards.note: Probarse is to try on; the pronoun is already present in me lo.

cards.translation: Where are the fitting rooms?
cards.note: Los probadores are fitting rooms.

cards.prompt: Me queda ___. Necesito una talla más grande.
cards.translation: It is too small on me. I need a larger size.
cards.note: Quedar describes how clothing fits.

cards.translation: The jacket fits me very well.
cards.note: Quedar bien means to fit or look good.

cards.translation: Can I pay by card?
cards.note: Pagar con tarjeta means to pay by card.
